subject: Request: short-term credit backfill & onramp credit for Novum pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <priya@novumanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@novumanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term credit backfill & onramp credit for Novum pilot

Hi Priyanka —

Quick note after reviewing your account: it looks like the Novum pilot exhausted the sandbox credits this morning. The engineering team saw good signal on the summary prompts (attached usage report), and I don't want the momentum to stall while procurement finishes the PO.

Would you accept a short-term "credit backfill" to restore the sandbox so your data scientists can finish the last evaluation week? My recommended approach: a one-time onramp credit (approx. 80k tokens / $5k equivalent) and a 30-day extension on the sandbox window. That should cover the remaining experiments and allow legal/procurement to complete the contract.

If procurement needs a formal ask: I'm happy to loop in our Sales Ops to prepare a short SOW and an interim invoice. Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood) apply a one-time credit today so Novum's sandbox resumes immediately.
- Sales Ops prepares a 30-day onramp SOW and sends to procurement for PO.
- Once PO/contract is signed we reconcile the credit against the initial invoice.

Attachments: novum_usage_summary_aug2026.csv (usage snapshot).

Can you confirm whether procurement will accept a short SOW + PO or if legal needs an NDA addendum?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Priyanka Rao <priya@novumanalytics.com>

Cc: procurement@novumanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term credit backfill & onramp credit for Novum pilot

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick check.

We did hit the limit this morning; the team was about to run a final batch of end-to-end tests. Procurement is copied here — we typically need a formal SOW and an estimate to open a PO. Legal will only flag major changes; a temporary credit and 30-day extension should be fine if it’s documented.

A couple questions from our side:
1) Can the credit be applied retroactively to the usage that pushed us over, or only forward-looking?
2) Who at Redwood will own the reconciliation once PO arrives?

If you can provide a short SOW and an interim invoice (even a placeholder), procurement can start the PO process today. We prefer credit applied immediately so the data team can keep going — they already made progress on the evaluation.

Thanks —
Priyanka Rao
Head of Data Science, Novum Analytics
priya@novumanalytics.com
